AyudaGrow / ExploreCreative review / three AI explainer concepts

One value proposition.
Three ways to bring it to life.

Explore different storytelling treatments for the website and social media. These are review concepts, not three new websites or published social posts.

01 / CONVERSATION FIRST

A customer asks.
The right next step follows.

Best for social: immediate human context, a visible answer and a clear handoff.

02 / KNOWLEDGE AT THE CENTRE

Your business knowledge.
Connected to useful answers.

Recommended website lead: makes customization and the connected system easy to understand.

03 / AFTER-HOURS CONTINUITY

A question tonight.
A prepared team tomorrow.

Best for a focused social story about time zones and out-of-office enquiries.

Different treatments can be selected for website and social. Motion is illustrative; performance, customer outcomes and availability are not guaranteed.

01 / Customer-conversation story

Lead with the customer’s question.

A simple conversation makes the benefit tangible: an enquiry, an answer grounded in approved knowledge, a configured next step and a person ready to continue.

Social adaptation: vertical message-led sequence, short opening question, answer and next step, ending on the brand and CTA. No real customer information.

02 / Business knowledge powering connected channels

Make the intelligence visible.

Approved information sits at the centre of the story. It supports useful answers across configured channels, while people maintain the knowledge and handle important decisions.

Website recommendation: use the clearest overview as the main explainer, with supporting copy below. Social adaptation: one knowledge source, three clear beats, then a human handoff.

03 / AI employee handling an after-hours enquiry

Keep momentum across the working day.

An enquiry arrives when the team is away. The assistant handles an agreed routine response and preserves the details for human follow-through.

Social adaptation: a day-to-night visual transition and one short enquiry story. Say “help customers outside working hours,” never “never miss a lead.”

My recommendation.

Lead the website with Knowledge at the centre to explain what makes the assistant specific to the business. Use Conversation first for the clearest social introduction. Develop After-hours continuity as a focused use-case story.

All three retain the same approved knowledge, configured actions, human handoff and reviewed-improvement boundaries.
